Hi Alex —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our discovery call:

1) SOC 2 / Compliance status
   - You mentioned FinHealth is undergoing SOC 2 Type II; estimated completion Q3 2026. Please confirm whether you have a SOC 2 Type I report we can review in the meantime.

2) Pen test report request
   - As discussed, our procurement/security team will need your most recent external penetration test report (redacted as needed). Can you share the latest PDF and the date of the engagement?

3) Vendor security questionnaire
   - We will start a vendor security questionnaire (standard InfoSec form). I attached our questionnaire stub for reference (redwood-security-questionnaire.pdf). If you prefer a shared link, let me know and I can send it through our secure collection form.

4) Vulnerability management expectations (proposal)
   - Triage SLA: acknowledge high/critical findings within 48 hours
   - Remediation SLA: critical = 7 days, high = 30 days, medium/low = agreed cadence
   - Scanning cadence: weekly external/unauthenticated scans + monthly authenticated scans; quarterly external pen tests (or after major releases)
   - Disclosure: coordinated disclosure window (7 days for critical) and contact for out-of-band escalations

Next steps / asks for you:
- Share the most recent pen test report (redacted) and the engagement date.
- Confirm SOC 2 status (Type I available?) or other relevant compliance artifacts.
- Confirm whether FinHealth will accept our vendor questionnaire link or prefers to return a PDF.
- Point of contact for vulnerability coordination/security (name/email).

I'll loop in our security lead (rishi_malhotra) once we have the report so they can review technical details and confirm SLAs. Monica (CC'd) will help with contract/procurement follow-ups.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping this moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks everyone — quick notes from the security side after a first pass of the redacted report: 

1) Scope/authentication
   - Please confirm whether RedCrest used authenticated scans for the API layer (test creds) or only unauthenticated external tests. Authenticated scan artifacts (session cookies/credentials scope) help surface logic flaws.

2) SLAs & cadence — proposed Redwood baseline (we can adjust once we see live environment):
   - Incident/Triage: acknowledge critical/high within 48 hours
   - Remediation targets: critical = 7 days, high = 30 days, medium = 90 days (or per mutually agreed plan)
   - Scanning cadence: weekly external unauthenticated + monthly authenticated + quarterly full external pen test OR after any production release that affects auth/billing/data flows
   - CVE handling: create a shared Jira board and a severity tagging convention; add FinHealth security as watchers for critical items

3) Disclosure policy
   - Recommend coordinated disclosure: 7 days for critical (remediation or agreed mitigation), 30 days for high before public disclosure. For anything PII-related we should use immediate out-of-band escalation.

4) Next technical steps
   - Alex: please provide (a) authenticated scan credentials (scoped read-only test account) and (b) RedCrest engagement contact. We can start a lightweight authenticated scan in our staging window once creds are provided.

I'll attach our VulnMgmt_SLA_Template.docx as a starting point for contractual language and service expectations. Monica — happy to sync on contract language you prefer for procurement.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Security Lead | Redwood Inference
